Programme Overview

The Cologne Graduate School of Ageing Research (CGA) in Germany is a joint venture of the University of Cologne Excellence Cluster on Stress Responses in Aging Associated Diseases (CECAD), the University Hospital Cologne, the Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing, and the Max Planck Institute for Metabolism Research. Cologne has emerged as a leading global research cluster with a stellar constellation of institutes and scientists dedicated to ageing research in Life Sciences. Up to 12 fully funded PhD positions are available for the 2027 cohort.

Research Areas

Our international, interdisciplinary faculty offers positions in cell or molecular biology, biochemistry, biophysics, bioinformatics, bioengineering, pharmacology, neuroscience, medical biology, translational medicine, or related fields.

What We Offer

  • An outstanding international research environment at one of Europe's most ageing research clusters, comprising 49 interdisciplinary research groups.
  • Initial work contracts of at least three years with payment based on the German TV-L E13 scale, 65% or on an equivalently remunerated PhD support contract of the Max Planck Society.
  • Dedicated supervision with academic guidance from thesis advisory committees.
  • Comprehensive PhD programme in the vibrant city of Cologne, conducted in English.
  • Individual career mentoring and coaching, wide range of methodology and soft skills courses.
  • Annual conference travel grants.
  • Intensive support and guidance for international students in all administrative matters.

Eligibility Criteria

  • Applicants with an MSc or equivalent degree in Biology, Cell/Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Bioengineering, Bioinformatics, Biophysics, Genetics, Medical Biology, Translational Medicine, or related fields.
  • Students with excellent academic performance in their BSc and MSc studies and a clear interest in the above-mentioned research areas, with strong motivation for ageing research.
  • Candidates with very good English skills (C1 level, written and spoken).
  • Applicants holding a medical degree are encouraged to apply, provided they demonstrate adequate relevant research experience.

Selection Procedure

  • Candidates will be evaluated based on their academic qualifications, research accomplishments, and motivation.
  • Up to 80 candidates will be selected to participate in online panel interviews scheduled for December 2026.
  • From these, up to 25 candidates will be invited to attend the recruitment week in Cologne in February 2027.
  • The PhD positions are anticipated to commence between July and October 2027.
  • All successful applicants will be enrolled through the University of Cologne.

Application Requirements

  • Statements regarding prior research experience and motivation for joining the programme.
  • Detailed research proposal outlining scientific interests and ideas.
  • Specification of three possible host laboratories.
  • Contact details of two academic advisors as referees (one should be your most recent supervisor).
  • CV, certificates, transcripts, and other supporting documents as separate PDF files.
  • Proficiency in both written and spoken English at a C1 level is essential. Submission of a formal language test certificate is not mandatory; alternatively, you may include a written statement outlining your reasons for considering yourself fluent in English.

Joseph-Stelzmann-Str. 9b/26
50931, Cologne, Germany
E-Mail: cga-coordination@uni-koeln.de

Important Notes

  • Up to 12 fully funded PhD positions.
  • Three-year work contracts with payment based on German TV-L E13 scale (65%) or equivalent Max Planck Society contract.
  • English is the working language.
  • C1 English proficiency required.
  • Projects for the CGA class of 2027 will be available from 11 August 2026.
